hero.title: Oil Rises as US–Iran Tensions Keep Global Energy Markets on Edge
hero.description: Oil prices have risen again as uncertainty over US–Iran diplomacy and the Strait of Hormuz continues. Iraq is entering a new security phase following the completion of the US military withdrawal, while Nigeria, Europe and wider African energy markets remain closely tied to global developments.

breaking: 🛢️ Brent crude rises to about $103.73 a barrel as US–Iran tensions continue.
🇺🇸🇮🇷 Qatar continues diplomatic efforts between Washington and Tehran, but no comprehensive peace agreement has been reached.
🇮🇶 The United States has completed the withdrawal of its remaining forces from Iraq after more than two decades of military presence.
🇳🇬 A Nigerian court has ordered the downstream petroleum regulator to continue issuing fuel-import licences to three oil marketers.
🇳🇬🇰🇪 Dangote and Kenya are moving ahead with the planned $16 billion Lamu refinery project.
🇪🇺 Europe is considering delaying new methane-reporting requirements for imported oil and gas amid energy-supply concerns.
🇨🇳🇪🇺 China has warned of a response if the European Union introduces new restrictions targeting Chinese companies or products.
🇺🇦 Belgium plans to transfer three F-16 fighter jets to Ukraine before the end of 2026, according to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
🇪🇹 Fighting and regional tensions are intensifying in northern Ethiopia, raising concerns about wider instability.
🇿🇦 South Africa's latest maize forecast points to a stronger 2025/26 harvest, although the latest Reuters-verified estimate is 4.5% above the previous season.

featured.title: Middle East Conflict Keeps Oil Markets Under Pressure
featured.content: Oil prices climbed on Wednesday after US President Donald Trump rejected reports that Washington was prepared to ease sanctions on Iran. Brent crude futures rose to about $103.73 a barrel, while Qatar continued efforts to mediate between the United States and Iran. The diplomatic channel remains open, but there is no confirmed comprehensive settlement. The continuing uncertainty around the Strait of Hormuz remains central to global energy markets.

articles.title: US–Iran Diplomacy Continues as Oil Prices Rise
articles.content: Qatar is continuing indirect diplomatic efforts between the United States and Iran as the conflict enters another stage. Iran has linked the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz to conditions including reduced US military pressure, while Washington has not confirmed a comprehensive settlement. Trump has denied reports that he was prepared to ease sanctions on Tehran. Brent crude rose to about $103.73 a barrel on Wednesday as traders assessed the risk of further supply disruption.

articles.title: Iraq Enters New Security Phase After US Withdrawal
articles.content: The United States has completed the withdrawal of its remaining forces from Iraq, ending more than two decades of American military presence that began with the 2003 invasion. The withdrawal was agreed under an earlier plan and has now been completed during a period of renewed regional conflict. Iraqi officials and analysts are assessing the security implications, including the ability of Iraqi forces to manage threats from armed groups and Islamic State.

articles.title: Global Bonds Face Heavy September Pressure
articles.content: Global bond markets are heading towards one of their weakest monthly performances in years. US 10-year Treasury yields have approached their highest levels since 2007, while persistent inflation concerns, government borrowing needs and geopolitical uncertainty continue to influence investors. The US dollar has strengthened during September, while the euro and British pound have weakened against it.

articles.title: US Offers Additional Strategic Petroleum Reserve Oil
articles.content: The United States has announced that it will offer loans of up to 40 million barrels of crude from its Strategic Petroleum Reserve as part of an international effort coordinated through the International Energy Agency. The move follows disruptions linked to the Iran conflict and comes as fuel prices remain elevated. The US reserve is now below 284 million barrels, its lowest level since 1982.

articles.title: Nigeria Court Orders Continued Fuel Import Licensing
articles.content: A Nigerian Federal High Court has ordered the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority to continue granting, issuing, extending, renewing or reissuing petroleum-product import licences to Matrix Energy, A.A. Rano and AYM Shafa, subject to statutory and regulatory requirements. The ruling comes amid a wider debate over competition between fuel importers and domestic refiners.

articles.title: Nigeria's Fuel Market Remains Exposed to Global Oil Prices
articles.content: Nigeria continues to face pressure from higher international energy prices. Recent market checks have put petrol around ₦1,400 per litre in Lagos and Abuja, with some northern locations reporting prices around ₦1,500, while diesel has exceeded ₦2,000 per litre in some areas. The situation illustrates that increased domestic refining capacity does not completely shield Nigeria from international crude-price movements.

articles.title: Dangote and Kenya Move Ahead With $16 Billion Lamu Refinery
articles.content: Aliko Dangote and Kenyan President William Ruto are scheduled to break ground on a planned $16 billion refinery in Lamu. The proposed facility is modelled on Dangote's 700,000-barrel-per-day Nigerian refinery and is targeted for completion around 2030. The project aims to reduce East Africa's dependence on imported refined petroleum products and strengthen regional energy supply. The project also faces questions around crude supply, infrastructure and environmental concerns, including a Kenyan court dispute involving parts of the proposed site.

articles.title: Dangote Refinery IPO Attracts Strong Investor Interest
articles.content: The Dangote Petroleum Refinery's ongoing share offering continues to attract strong interest from Nigerian investors. Reuters reported that demand has been described as enormous, with some financial technology platforms experiencing significant increases in activity after the offering opened. The IPO is linked to plans to expand the refinery's capacity, while the wider business is increasingly involved in international refined-fuel markets. Investors should remember that strong demand does not guarantee future investment returns.

articles.title: Ethiopia Faces Renewed Tigray Security Crisis
articles.content: Fighting and political tensions have intensified in northern Ethiopia's Tigray region. Regional forces have seized strategic locations and clashes have raised concerns about a return to wider conflict. Ethiopian authorities have also accused regional rivals of supporting armed groups, allegations that affected countries may dispute. The situation is being closely watched because of the existing tensions involving Ethiopia, Eritrea and Sudan.

articles.title: South Africa Expects Stronger Maize Harvest
articles.content: South Africa's 2025/26 maize harvest is projected to be higher than the previous season. The latest Reuters-verified government forecast puts production at about 17.4 million metric tonnes, approximately 4.5% above the previous season. The stronger harvest could support food supplies and agricultural markets, although wider energy and economic pressures remain important for consumers.

articles.title: Europe Reviews Energy Rules Amid Supply Concerns
articles.content: The European Union is considering delaying new methane-emissions requirements for oil and gas imports because governments are concerned that the rules could complicate energy supplies during a period of high prices and geopolitical disruption. The International Energy Agency is also monitoring global oil markets and says member countries remain prepared to consider further strategic-stock measures if necessary.

articles.title: China Warns EU Over Possible Trade Restrictions
articles.content: China has warned that it would respond if the European Union introduces measures targeting Chinese companies or products. Beijing's warning follows discussion among EU member states about a proposed tool intended to address what some governments regard as unfair competition. The dispute adds another layer to the wider EU–China economic relationship.

articles.title: Belgium Plans Three F-16 Transfers to Ukraine
articles.content: Ukraine says Belgium plans to transfer three F-16 fighter jets before the end of 2026. The announcement comes as European countries continue to discuss military and financial assistance for Ukraine during the continuing war with Russia.

articles.title: Washington Continues Pressure on Iran While Qatar Mediates
articles.content: The United States continues to apply economic and military pressure on Iran while Qatar works as an intermediary between Washington and Tehran. The diplomatic effort has so far produced no comprehensive peace agreement. The Strait of Hormuz remains a central issue because disruption there can affect global oil and shipping markets.

articles.title: China–EU Technology and Trade Tensions Continue
articles.content: Trade tensions between China and the European Union are increasingly linked to technology, industrial competition and market access. Beijing has warned of countermeasures if Brussels moves ahead with restrictions targeting Chinese companies or products. The issue comes as Europe also reviews the security and cost implications of Chinese technology in sensitive infrastructure.

morningSummary: The global picture this morning is dominated by energy security, US–Iran diplomacy and the economic consequences of prolonged geopolitical tensions. Oil has risen above $103 a barrel as uncertainty surrounding Iran and the Strait of Hormuz persists. The United States has completed its withdrawal from Iraq, while Qatar continues diplomatic efforts between Washington and Tehran. In Africa, Nigeria's fuel market, the Dangote refinery IPO and the planned $16 billion Kenya refinery remain major economic stories. Europe is balancing energy security with environmental and trade policies, while China–EU commercial tensions continue.
bigQuestion: As global energy prices remain closely tied to events in the Middle East, how can countries protect ordinary households and businesses from another major rise in the cost of living?
